records.literal_gloss: And said Leah, in my happiness, for call me happy daughters; and she called his name Asher.

en.L: And Leah said, "In my happiness! For daughters will call me happy." And she called his name Asher.
en.B: Leah said, "Happy am I! Women everywhere will speak of my happiness." So she named him Asher.
en.R: Leah said, "I am so happy! Now the other women will say how happy I am." So she named him Asher, which means "happy."

es.L: Y dijo Lea: «¡En mi dicha! Porque las hijas me llamarán dichosa». Y llamó su nombre Aser.
es.B: Lea dijo: «¡Qué dichosa soy! Todas las mujeres hablarán de mi dicha». Así que lo llamó Aser.
es.R: Lea dijo: «¡Qué feliz soy! Ahora las demás mujeres dirán lo feliz que soy». Por eso lo llamó Aser, que quiere decir «feliz».

fr.L: Et Léa dit : « Pour mon bonheur ! Car les filles me diront heureuse. » Et elle appela son nom Aser.
fr.B: Léa dit : « Que je suis heureuse ! Partout, les femmes parleront de mon bonheur. » Elle le nomma donc Aser.
fr.R: Léa a dit : « Je suis si heureuse ! Maintenant, les autres femmes diront combien je suis heureuse. » Alors elle l’a appelé Aser, ce qui veut dire « heureux ».

sw.L: Lea akasema, "Katika furaha yangu! Kwa kuwa binti wataniita mwenye heri." Akamwita jina lake Asheri.
sw.B: Lea akasema, "Nina furaha kweli! Wanawake kila mahali watazungumza juu ya furaha yangu." Basi akamwita Asheri.
sw.R: Lea akasema, "Nina furaha sana! Sasa wanawake wengine watasema jinsi nilivyo na furaha." Basi akamwita Asheri, maana yake "mwenye furaha."

decisions.choice: Asher: "happy", a pun on be'oshri, "in my happiness", and ishsheruni, "they call me happy"
decisions.reason: The name and both of Leah's words come from the root ashar, "happy" or "fortunate", the word that begins Psalm 1 ("Happy is the one ..."). Leah's joy is in the honor other women will give her.

decisions.choice: daughters: women
decisions.reason: "Daughters" here means women in general, as in Song of Songs 6:9.

decisions.choice: Women (B); the other women (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "daughters" (m2).

decisions.choice: which means "happy"
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name (m1).

source.text: וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ רְאוּבֵ֜ן בִּימֵ֣י קְצִיר־חִטִּ֗ים וַיִּמְצָ֤א דֽוּדָאִים֙ בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה וַיָּבֵ֣א אֹתָ֔ם אֶל־לֵאָ֖ה אִמּ֑וֹ וַתֹּ֤אמֶר רָחֵל֙ אֶל־לֵאָ֔ה תְּנִי־נָ֣א לִ֔י מִדּוּדָאֵ֖י בְּנֵֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And went Reuben in [the] days of [the] harvest of wheat and found mandrakes in the field, and he brought them to Leah his mother; and said Rachel to Leah, give please to me some of [the] mandrakes of your son.

en.L: And Reuben went in the days of the wheat harvest and found mandrakes in the field and brought them to Leah his mother. And Rachel said to Leah, "Please give me some of your son's mandrakes."
en.B: At wheat harvest time Reuben was out in the fields and came upon some mandrakes, which he brought home to his mother Leah. Rachel asked Leah, "Please let me have some of the mandrakes your son found."
en.R: When the wheat was being harvested, Reuben found some mandrake plants in a field. He took them to his mother Leah. Rachel said to Leah, "Please share your son's mandrakes with me."

es.L: Y fue Rubén en los días de la siega del trigo, y halló mandrágoras en el campo, y las trajo a Lea su madre. Y dijo Raquel a Lea: «Dame, por favor, de las mandrágoras de tu hijo».
es.B: En tiempo de la cosecha del trigo, Rubén salió al campo y encontró unas mandrágoras, que llevó a su madre Lea. Raquel le pidió a Lea: «Por favor, dame algunas de las mandrágoras que encontró tu hijo».
es.R: Cuando estaban cosechando el trigo, Rubén encontró unas plantas de mandrágora en un campo. Se las llevó a su madre Lea. Raquel le dijo a Lea: «Por favor, comparte conmigo las mandrágoras de tu hijo».

fr.L: Et Ruben alla, aux jours de la moisson du blé, et il trouva des mandragores dans les champs, et il les apporta à Léa, sa mère. Et Rachel dit à Léa : « Donne-moi, je te prie, des mandragores de ton fils. »
fr.B: Au temps de la moisson du blé, Ruben, qui était aux champs, trouva des mandragores et les rapporta à sa mère Léa. Rachel demanda à Léa : « S’il te plaît, donne-moi quelques-unes des mandragores que ton fils a trouvées. »
fr.R: Pendant qu’on moissonnait le blé, Ruben a trouvé des mandragores dans un champ. Il les a apportées à sa mère Léa. Rachel a dit à Léa : « S’il te plaît, partage avec moi les mandragores de ton fils. »

sw.L: Reubeni alikwenda siku za mavuno ya ngano, akapata tunguja kondeni, akazileta kwa Lea mama yake. Raheli akamwambia Lea, "Tafadhali nipe baadhi ya tunguja za mwanao."
sw.B: Wakati wa mavuno ya ngano Reubeni alikuwa shambani, akaona tunguja, akampelekea mama yake Lea. Raheli akamwomba Lea, "Tafadhali nipe baadhi ya tunguja alizoleta mwanao."
sw.R: Watu walipokuwa wakivuna ngano, Reubeni aliona mimea ya tunguja shambani. Akampelekea mama yake Lea. Raheli akamwambia Lea, "Tafadhali nigawie tunguja za mwanao."

decisions.choice: mandrakes: a plant thought to help a woman conceive
decisions.reason: The mandrake has a forked root and fragrant yellow fruit that ripens at wheat harvest, in late spring. In the ancient world it was believed to arouse love and to help childless women conceive. Its name (duda'im) sounds like dodim, "love" (Song of Songs 7:13). Rachel wants it as a fertility charm; in the end it is God who opens her womb (verse 22).

decisions.choice: Reuben: still a boy
decisions.reason: Reuben was Leah's oldest son, and only a few years old at this point. It is natural that a child picking in the fields would bring his find to his mother.

decisions.choice: "tunguja"
decisions.reason: Swahili has no everyday name for the mandrake; "tunguja" names a related plant of the nightshade family and is the long-used Swahili word for the duda'im. Readable says "mimea ya tunguja" so it is clear a plant is meant. A reviewer may prefer another word.

source.text: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר לָ֗הּ הַמְעַט֙ קַחְתֵּ֣ךְ אֶת־אִישִׁ֔י וְלָקַ֕חַת גַּ֥ם אֶת־דּוּדָאֵ֖י בְּנִ֑י וַתֹּ֣אמֶר רָחֵ֗ל לָכֵן֙ יִשְׁכַּ֤ב עִמָּךְ֙ הַלַּ֔יְלָה תַּ֖חַת דּוּדָאֵ֥י בְנֵֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And she said to her, [is it] a small thing your taking my husband, and [you would] take also [the] mandrakes of my son? And said Rachel, therefore he will lie with you tonight in exchange for [the] mandrakes of your son.

en.L: But she said to her, "Is it a small matter that you have taken my husband? Would you take my son's mandrakes too?" And Rachel said, "Then he shall lie with you tonight in exchange for your son's mandrakes."
en.B: But Leah answered, "Is it a small thing to you that you have taken my husband? And now you would take my son's mandrakes too?" Rachel said, "Then Jacob may sleep with you tonight; that is the price of your son's mandrakes."
en.R: But Leah said, "You have already taken my husband away from me. Now you want to take my son's mandrakes too?" Rachel said, "All right. If you give me your son's mandrakes, Jacob can sleep with you tonight."

es.L: Y ella le dijo: «¿Es poca cosa que me hayas quitado a mi marido, y quieras quitar también las mandrágoras de mi hijo?». Y dijo Raquel: «Por tanto, él se acostará contigo esta noche a cambio de las mandrágoras de tu hijo».
es.B: Pero Lea respondió: «¿Te parece poco haberme quitado a mi marido? ¿Y ahora también quieres quitarme las mandrágoras de mi hijo?». Raquel dijo: «Entonces que Jacob duerma contigo esta noche; ese será el precio de las mandrágoras de tu hijo».
es.R: Pero Lea le dijo: «Ya me quitaste a mi marido. ¿Ahora también quieres quitarme las mandrágoras de mi hijo?». Raquel dijo: «Está bien. Si me das las mandrágoras de tu hijo, Jacob puede dormir contigo esta noche».

fr.L: Mais elle lui dit : « Est-ce peu de chose que tu aies pris mon mari ? Et tu prendrais aussi les mandragores de mon fils ? » Et Rachel dit : « Eh bien, il couchera avec toi cette nuit, en échange des mandragores de ton fils. »
fr.B: Mais Léa répondit : « Ne te suffit-il pas de m’avoir pris mon mari ? Faut-il encore que tu prennes les mandragores de mon fils ? » Rachel dit : « Alors Jacob couchera avec toi cette nuit ; ce sera le prix des mandragores de ton fils. »
fr.R: Mais Léa a dit : « Tu m’as déjà pris mon mari. Et maintenant, tu veux aussi prendre les mandragores de mon fils ? » Rachel a dit : « D’accord. Si tu me donnes les mandragores de ton fils, Jacob pourra dormir avec toi cette nuit. »

sw.L: Akamwambia, "Je, ni jambo dogo kwamba umemchukua mume wangu? Nawe utachukua pia tunguja za mwanangu?" Raheli akasema, "Basi atalala nawe usiku huu badala ya tunguja za mwanao."
sw.B: Lakini Lea akajibu, "Je, ni jambo dogo kwako kwamba umemchukua mume wangu? Sasa unataka kuchukua pia tunguja za mwanangu?" Raheli akasema, "Basi Yakobo atalala nawe usiku huu; hiyo ndiyo bei ya tunguja za mwanao."
sw.R: Lakini Lea akasema, "Tayari umeninyang'anya mume wangu. Sasa unataka kuchukua tunguja za mwanangu pia?" Raheli akasema, "Sawa. Ukinipa tunguja za mwanao, Yakobo atalala nawe usiku wa leo."

decisions.choice: you have taken my husband: Jacob lived with Rachel
decisions.reason: Jacob loved Rachel more (29:30), and it seems he spent his nights in her tent. Leah, though the first wife, feels her husband has been taken from her. Rachel has the power to decide whose tent Jacob sleeps in that night.

decisions.choice: Jacob
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jacob, so it is clear who "he" is.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֨א יַעֲקֹ֣ב מִן־הַשָּׂדֶה֮ בָּעֶרֶב֒ וַתֵּצֵ֨א לֵאָ֜ה לִקְרָאת֗וֹ וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֵלַ֣י תָּב֔וֹא כִּ֚י שָׂכֹ֣ר שְׂכַרְתִּ֔יךָ בְּדוּדָאֵ֖י בְּנִ֑י וַיִּשְׁכַּ֥ב עִמָּ֖הּ בַּלַּ֥יְלָה הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: And came Jacob from the field in the evening, and went out Leah to meet him and said, to me you will come in, for surely I have hired you with [the] mandrakes of my son; and he lay with her that night.

en.L: And Jacob came from the field in the evening, and Leah went out to meet him and said, "You must come in to me, for I have surely hired you with my son's mandrakes." So he lay with her that night.
en.B: That evening, as Jacob was coming in from the fields, Leah went out to him and said, "Tonight you are coming to me. I have paid for you with my son's mandrakes." And he spent that night with her.
en.R: In the evening Jacob came back from the fields. Leah met him on the way and said, "You will sleep in my tent tonight. I paid for you with my son's mandrakes." So that night Jacob slept with her.

es.L: Y vino Jacob del campo por la tarde, y salió Lea a su encuentro y dijo: «Conmigo has de entrar, porque ciertamente te he alquilado con las mandrágoras de mi hijo». Y se acostó con ella aquella noche.
es.B: Por la tarde, cuando Jacob volvía del campo, Lea salió a su encuentro y le dijo: «Esta noche vas a dormir conmigo. He pagado por ti con las mandrágoras de mi hijo». Y él pasó aquella noche con ella.
es.R: Por la tarde Jacob volvió del campo. Lea salió a encontrarlo y le dijo: «Esta noche vas a dormir en mi tienda. Pagué por ti con las mandrágoras de mi hijo». Así que esa noche Jacob durmió con ella.

fr.L: Et Jacob revint des champs le soir, et Léa sortit à sa rencontre et dit : « C’est vers moi que tu viendras, car je t’ai bel et bien loué avec les mandragores de mon fils. » Et il coucha avec elle cette nuit-là.
fr.B: Le soir, comme Jacob rentrait des champs, Léa sortit au-devant de lui et lui dit : « Cette nuit, c’est chez moi que tu viens. Je t’ai payé avec les mandragores de mon fils. » Et il passa cette nuit-là avec elle.
fr.R: Le soir, Jacob est revenu des champs. Léa est allée à sa rencontre et lui a dit : « Cette nuit, tu dormiras dans ma tente. J’ai payé pour toi avec les mandragores de mon fils. » Alors, cette nuit-là, Jacob a couché avec elle.

sw.L: Yakobo akaja kutoka shambani jioni, naye Lea akatoka kumlaki, akasema, "Utaingia kwangu, kwa maana hakika nimekuajiri kwa tunguja za mwanangu." Akalala naye usiku ule.
sw.B: Jioni Yakobo alipokuwa akirudi kutoka shambani, Lea akatoka kumlaki, akasema, "Usiku huu utakuja kwangu. Nimekulipia kwa tunguja za mwanangu." Naye akalala naye usiku ule.
sw.R: Jioni Yakobo alirudi kutoka shambani. Lea akakutana naye njiani, akasema, "Leo usiku utalala hemani mwangu. Nimekulipia kwa tunguja za mwanangu." Basi usiku ule Yakobo akalala naye.

decisions.choice: I have surely hired you: Leah paid for the night
decisions.reason: The verb (sakhar) is used of hiring a worker for wages, and it is repeated for emphasis ("hire, I have hired"). It prepares the name Issachar in verse 18. Jacob, who worked for wages for his wives (29:15), is now himself hired.

decisions.choice: paid for you
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "paid for", which carries the sense of hiring in natural English; Literal keeps "hired" so the link with Issachar can be seen.

decisions.choice: "te he alquilado"
decisions.reason: "Contratar" is the ordinary word for hiring a worker but sounds like an employment contract; "alquilar" keeps the starkness of paying for a man's night and the link with the wage ("salario") of verse 18.

decisions.choice: "je t'ai bel et bien loué"
decisions.reason: "Louer" a person is to hire them for a wage, which is the verb's sense; "bel et bien" renders the doubled Hebrew verb. "Acheter" would say more than hiring.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֥ע אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶל־לֵאָ֑ה וַתַּ֛הַר וַתֵּ֥לֶד לְיַעֲקֹ֖ב בֵּ֥ן חֲמִישִֽׁי׃

records.literal_gloss: And listened God to Leah, and she conceived and bore to Jacob a son fifth.

en.L: And God listened to Leah, and she conceived and bore Jacob a fifth son.
en.B: God heard Leah's prayer. She conceived and gave Jacob a fifth son.
en.R: God answered Leah's prayers. She became pregnant and had a fifth son for Jacob.

es.L: Y Dios escuchó a Lea, y ella concibió y dio a luz a Jacob un quinto hijo.
es.B: Dios escuchó la oración de Lea. Ella concibió y le dio a Jacob un quinto hijo.
es.R: Dios respondió a las oraciones de Lea. Ella quedó embarazada y tuvo un quinto hijo para Jacob.

fr.L: Et Dieu écouta Léa, et elle conçut et enfanta à Jacob un cinquième fils.
fr.B: Dieu exauça la prière de Léa. Elle conçut et donna à Jacob un cinquième fils.
fr.R: Dieu a répondu aux prières de Léa. Elle est tombée enceinte et elle a eu un cinquième fils pour Jacob.

sw.L: Mungu akamsikiliza Lea, naye akapata mimba, akamzalia Yakobo mwana wa tano.
sw.B: Mungu alisikia maombi ya Lea. Akapata mimba, akamzalia Yakobo mwana wa tano.
sw.R: Mungu alijibu maombi ya Lea. Akapata mimba, akamzalia Yakobo mtoto wa tano wa kiume.

decisions.choice: God listened to Leah: the child is God's answer
decisions.reason: The text does not credit the mandrakes. It says God listened, which implies Leah had prayed. Rachel had the mandrakes, but Leah had the child.

decisions.choice: heard Leah's prayer (B); answered Leah's prayers (R)
decisions.reason: "Listened to" someone, said of God, means he heard and answered a request; Balanced and Readable say so.

source.text: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר לֵאָ֗ה נָתַ֤ן אֱלֹהִים֙ שְׂכָרִ֔י אֲשֶׁר־נָתַ֥תִּי שִׁפְחָתִ֖י לְאִישִׁ֑י וַתִּקְרָ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ יִשָּׂשכָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Leah, has given God my wage, because I gave my slave woman to my husband; and she called his name Issachar.

en.L: And Leah said, "God has given me my wages, because I gave my slave woman to my husband." So she called his name Issachar.
en.B: Leah said, "God has given me my wages for giving my servant to my husband." So she named him Issachar.
en.R: Leah said, "God has paid me back because I gave my servant to my husband." So she named him Issachar, which means "reward."

es.L: Y dijo Lea: «Dios me ha dado mi salario, porque di mi esclava a mi marido». Y llamó su nombre Isacar.
es.B: Lea dijo: «Dios me ha pagado mi salario por haberle dado mi sierva a mi marido». Así que lo llamó Isacar.
es.R: Lea dijo: «Dios me lo ha pagado, porque le di mi sierva a mi marido». Por eso lo llamó Isacar, que quiere decir «recompensa».

fr.L: Et Léa dit : « Dieu m’a donné mon salaire, parce que j’ai donné mon esclave à mon mari. » Et elle appela son nom Issacar.
fr.B: Léa dit : « Dieu m’a payé mon salaire pour avoir donné ma servante à mon mari. » Elle le nomma donc Issacar.
fr.R: Léa a dit : « Dieu m’a récompensée parce que j’ai donné ma servante à mon mari. » Alors elle l’a appelé Issacar, ce qui veut dire « récompense ».

sw.L: Lea akasema, "Mungu amenipa ujira wangu, kwa sababu nilimpa mume wangu mtumwa wangu." Akamwita jina lake Isakari.
sw.B: Lea akasema, "Mungu amenipa ujira wangu kwa kumpa mume wangu mtumishi wangu." Basi akamwita Isakari.
sw.R: Lea akasema, "Mungu amenilipa kwa sababu nilimpa mume wangu mtumishi wangu." Basi akamwita Isakari, maana yake "ujira."

decisions.choice: Issachar: "there is a reward" or "man of wages", a pun on sakhar, "wage"
decisions.reason: The name contains sakhar, "wage" or "hire". It echoes Leah's words to Jacob, "I have hired you" (verse 16), and here her own reason: God has paid her a wage for giving Zilpah to Jacob. Both puns stand together in the name.

decisions.choice: paid me back (R)
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plain verb for paying, keeping the idea of a wage.

decisions.choice: which means "reward"
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name (m1).

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave".

source.text: וַתַּ֤הַר עוֹד֙ לֵאָ֔ה וַתֵּ֥לֶד בֵּן־שִׁשִּׁ֖י לְּיַעֲקֹֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: And conceived again Leah and bore a son sixth to Jacob.

en.L: And Leah conceived again and bore Jacob a sixth son.
en.B: Once more Leah became pregnant, and she bore Jacob a sixth son.
en.R: Leah became pregnant again and had a sixth son for Jacob.

es.L: Y concibió otra vez Lea y dio a luz un sexto hijo a Jacob.
es.B: Lea quedó embarazada una vez más y le dio a Jacob un sexto hijo.
es.R: Lea quedó embarazada otra vez y tuvo un sexto hijo para Jacob.

fr.L: Et Léa conçut encore et enfanta un sixième fils à Jacob.
fr.B: Léa devint enceinte une fois de plus et donna à Jacob un sixième fils.
fr.R: Léa est encore tombée enceinte et elle a eu un sixième fils pour Jacob.

sw.L: Lea akapata mimba tena, akamzalia Yakobo mwana wa sita.
sw.B: Lea alipata mimba mara nyingine, akamzalia Yakobo mwana wa sita.
sw.R: Lea alipata mimba tena, akamzalia Yakobo mtoto wa sita wa kiume.

source.text: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר לֵאָ֗ה זְבָדַ֨נִי אֱלֹהִ֥ים׀אֹתִי֮ זֵ֣בֶד טוֹב֒ הַפַּ֨עַם֙ יִזְבְּלֵ֣נִי אִישִׁ֔י כִּֽי־יָלַ֥דְתִּי ל֖וֹ שִׁשָּׁ֣ה בָנִ֑ים וַתִּקְרָ֥א אֶת־שְׁמ֖וֹ זְבֻלֽוּן׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Leah, has endowed me God [with] an endowment good; this time will honor me my husband, for I have borne to him six sons; and she called his name Zebulun.

en.L: And Leah said, "God has endowed me with a good endowment; now my husband will honor me, because I have borne him six sons." So she called his name Zebulun.
en.B: Leah said, "God has endowed me with a rich gift. Now at last my husband will honor me, since I have borne him six sons." So she named him Zebulun.
en.R: Leah said, "God has given me a wonderful gift. Now my husband will respect me, because I have had six sons for him." So she named him Zebulun, which means "honor."

es.L: Y dijo Lea: «Dios me ha dotado con una buena dote; esta vez mi marido me honrará, porque le he dado a luz seis hijos». Y llamó su nombre Zabulón.
es.B: Lea dijo: «Dios me ha dotado con un regalo valioso. Ahora por fin mi marido me honrará, pues le he dado seis hijos». Así que lo llamó Zabulón.
es.R: Lea dijo: «Dios me ha dado un regalo maravilloso. Ahora mi marido me respetará, porque le he dado seis hijos». Por eso lo llamó Zabulón, que quiere decir «honra».

fr.L: Et Léa dit : « Dieu m’a dotée d’une belle dot ; cette fois mon mari m’honorera, car je lui ai enfanté six fils. » Et elle appela son nom Zabulon.
fr.B: Léa dit : « Dieu m’a fait un riche cadeau. Cette fois, mon mari m’honorera enfin, puisque je lui ai donné six fils. » Elle le nomma donc Zabulon.
fr.R: Léa a dit : « Dieu m’a fait un cadeau magnifique. Maintenant, mon mari va me respecter, car je lui ai donné six fils. » Alors elle l’a appelé Zabulon, ce qui veut dire « honneur ».

sw.L: Lea akasema, "Mungu amenijalia zawadi njema; wakati huu mume wangu ataniheshimu, kwa sababu nimemzalia wana sita." Akamwita jina lake Zabuloni.
sw.B: Lea akasema, "Mungu amenipa zawadi ya thamani. Sasa hatimaye mume wangu ataniheshimu, kwa kuwa nimemzalia wana sita." Basi akamwita Zabuloni.
sw.R: Lea akasema, "Mungu amenipa zawadi nzuri sana. Sasa mume wangu ataniheshimu, kwa sababu nimemzalia watoto sita wa kiume." Basi akamwita Zabuloni, maana yake "heshima."

decisions.choice: Zebulun: a double pun, on zebed, "gift", and yizbeleni, "he will honor me"
decisions.reason: Leah's first words, "God has endowed me with an endowment" (zebadani ... zebed), sound like the name. Her second, yizbeleni, sounds like it even more closely.

decisions.choice: he will honor me: or "he will live with me"
decisions.reason: The verb (zabal) is rare. A related noun means a lofty dwelling (1 Kings 8:13), and the verb may mean to honor, or to live with someone as a husband. Either way Leah hopes at last for Jacob's regard (29:32, 34).

decisions.choice: which means "honor"
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name by Leah's second pun (m1, m2).

source.text: וְאַחַ֖ר יָ֣לְדָה בַּ֑ת וַתִּקְרָ֥א אֶת־שְׁמָ֖הּ דִּינָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And afterward she bore a daughter and called her name Dinah.

en.L: And afterward she bore a daughter and called her name Dinah.
en.B: Afterward she had a daughter, whom she named Dinah.
en.R: Later Leah had a daughter and named her Dinah.

es.L: Y después dio a luz una hija y llamó su nombre Dina.
es.B: Después tuvo una hija, a la que llamó Dina.
es.R: Más tarde Lea tuvo una hija y le puso por nombre Dina.

fr.L: Et ensuite elle enfanta une fille et appela son nom Dina.
fr.B: Ensuite elle eut une fille, qu’elle nomma Dina.
fr.R: Plus tard, Léa a eu une fille et elle l’a appelée Dina.

sw.L: Baadaye akazaa binti, akamwita jina lake Dina.
sw.B: Baadaye alizaa binti, akamwita Dina.
sw.R: Baadaye Lea alizaa mtoto wa kike, akampa jina Dina.

decisions.choice: Dinah: "judgment" or "vindicated", with no reason given
decisions.reason: Unlike her brothers' names, Dinah's is not explained. It comes from the same root as Dan (din, "judge", verse 6). She is mentioned because of what happens to her in chapter 34. Jacob had other daughters too (37:35; 46:7).

source.text: וַיִּזְכֹּ֥ר אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶת־רָחֵ֑ל וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע אֵלֶ֨יהָ֙ אֱלֹהִ֔ים וַיִּפְתַּ֖ח אֶת־רַחְמָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And remembered God Rachel, and listened to her God, and opened her womb.

en.L: Then God remembered Rachel, and God listened to her and opened her womb.
en.B: Then God remembered Rachel. He heard her prayers and opened her womb.
en.R: Then God remembered Rachel. He answered her prayers and made it possible for her to have children.

es.L: Entonces Dios se acordó de Raquel, y Dios la escuchó y abrió su matriz.
es.B: Entonces Dios se acordó de Raquel. Escuchó sus oraciones y le abrió el vientre.
es.R: Entonces Dios se acordó de Raquel. Respondió a sus oraciones e hizo posible que tuviera hijos.

fr.L: Alors Dieu se souvint de Rachel, et Dieu l’écouta et ouvrit son sein.
fr.B: Alors Dieu se souvint de Rachel. Il exauça ses prières et ouvrit son sein.
fr.R: Alors Dieu s’est souvenu de Rachel. Il a répondu à ses prières et lui a permis d’avoir des enfants.

sw.L: Kisha Mungu akamkumbuka Raheli, naye Mungu akamsikiliza, akalifungua tumbo lake.
sw.B: Kisha Mungu alimkumbuka Raheli. Akasikia maombi yake, akalifungua tumbo lake.
sw.R: Kisha Mungu alimkumbuka Raheli. Akajibu maombi yake, akamwezesha kupata watoto.

decisions.choice: God remembered: God acted on Rachel's behalf
decisions.reason: When God "remembers" someone, he does not recall what he had forgotten; he turns to act for them, as he remembered Noah (8:1) and Abraham (19:29), and later Hannah (1 Samuel 1:19).

decisions.choice: opened her womb: what God did for Leah
decisions.reason: The same words are used of Leah in 29:31, where Rachel was barren. Rachel's child comes from God, not from the mandrakes she bargained for (verse 14).

decisions.choice: made it possible for her to have children
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture.

source.text: וַתַּ֖הַר וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֑ן וַתֹּ֕אמֶר אָסַ֥ף אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶת־חֶרְפָּתִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And she conceived and bore a son and said, has taken away God my reproach.

en.L: And she conceived and bore a son and said, "God has taken away my reproach."
en.B: She conceived and bore a son, and she said, "God has removed my shame."
en.R: Rachel became pregnant and had a son. "God has taken my shame away," she said.

es.L: Y ella concibió y dio a luz un hijo, y dijo: «Dios ha quitado mi afrenta».
es.B: Ella concibió y dio a luz un hijo, y dijo: «Dios ha borrado mi vergüenza».
es.R: Raquel quedó embarazada y tuvo un hijo. «Dios me ha quitado la vergüenza», dijo.

fr.L: Et elle conçut et enfanta un fils, et dit : « Dieu a enlevé mon opprobre. »
fr.B: Elle conçut et enfanta un fils, et elle dit : « Dieu a ôté ma honte. »
fr.R: Rachel est tombée enceinte et elle a eu un fils. « Dieu m’a enlevé ma honte », a-t-elle dit.

sw.L: Akapata mimba, akazaa mwana, akasema, "Mungu ameiondoa aibu yangu."
sw.B: Alipata mimba, akazaa mwana, akasema, "Mungu ameniondolea aibu yangu."
sw.R: Raheli alipata mimba, akazaa mtoto wa kiume. Akasema, "Mungu ameniondolea aibu."

decisions.choice: God has taken away (asaf) my reproach: the first pun on Joseph
decisions.reason: Rachel's first saying plays on the name Joseph with the verb asaf, "gather in" or "take away". Her second (verse 24) uses yasaf, "add". Childlessness was a public disgrace for a wife (1 Samuel 1:6; Luke 1:25).

source.text: וַתִּקְרָ֧א אֶת־שְׁמ֛וֹ יוֹסֵ֖ף לֵאמֹ֑ר יֹסֵ֧ף יְהוָ֛ה לִ֖י בֵּ֥ן אַחֵֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And she called his name Joseph, saying, may add YHWH to me a son another.

en.L: And she called his name Joseph, saying, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} add to me another son!"
en.B: She called him Joseph, for she said, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} add one more son to me."
en.R: She named him Joseph, which means "may he add," because she said, "I pray {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will give me one more son."

es.L: Y llamó su nombre José, diciendo: «¡Que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me añada otro hijo!».
es.B: Lo llamó José, pues dijo: «Que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me añada un hijo más».
es.R: Le puso por nombre José, que quiere decir «que él añada», porque dijo: «Le pido {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} que me dé un hijo más».

fr.L: Et elle appela son nom Joseph, disant : « Que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} m’ajoute un autre fils ! »
fr.B: Elle l’appela Joseph, car elle dit : « Que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} m’ajoute encore un fils. »
fr.R: Elle l’a appelé Joseph, ce qui veut dire « qu’il ajoute », parce qu’elle a dit : « Je prie {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} de me donner encore un fils. »

sw.L: Akamwita jina lake Yusufu, akisema, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na aniongeze mwana mwingine!"
sw.B: Akamwita Yusufu, kwa maana alisema, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na aniongezee mwana mmoja zaidi."
sw.R: Akampa jina Yusufu, maana yake "na aongeze," kwa sababu alisema, "Ninamwomba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} anipe mwana mmoja zaidi."

decisions.choice: Joseph: "may he add", a pun on yosef, "may he add"
decisions.reason: The name is a verb form, "may he add" (yasaf). With asaf, "he has taken away" (verse 23), Rachel's two sayings give the name two senses: God has taken away her shame, and she prays he will add another son. The prayer is answered in Benjamin (35:16-18).

decisions.choice: which means "may he add"
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name (m1).

source.text: וַיְהִ֕י כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר יָלְדָ֥ה רָחֵ֖ל אֶת־יוֹסֵ֑ף וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יַעֲקֹב֙ אֶל־לָבָ֔ן שַׁלְּחֵ֨נִי֙ וְאֵ֣לְכָ֔ה אֶל־מְקוֹמִ֖י וּלְאַרְצִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when had borne Rachel Joseph, and said Jacob to Laban, send me away, that I may go to my place and to my land.

en.L: And when Rachel had borne Joseph, Jacob said to Laban, "Send me away, that I may go to my own place and to my land.
en.B: After Rachel had given birth to Joseph, Jacob said to Laban, "Let me go now, so that I can return to my own home and country.
en.R: After Rachel had Joseph, Jacob said to Laban, "Let me leave now. I want to go back to my own home and my own country.

es.L: Y sucedió que, cuando Raquel hubo dado a luz a José, Jacob dijo a Labán: «Despídeme, para que me vaya a mi lugar y a mi tierra.
es.B: Después de que Raquel dio a luz a José, Jacob le dijo a Labán: «Déjame ir ya, para que pueda volver a mi propia casa y a mi país.
es.R: Después de que Raquel tuvo a José, Jacob le dijo a Labán: «Déjame irme ya. Quiero volver a mi casa y a mi país.

fr.L: Et il arriva, lorsque Rachel eut enfanté Joseph, que Jacob dit à Laban : « Renvoie-moi, et que je m’en aille vers mon lieu et vers mon pays.
fr.B: Après que Rachel eut donné naissance à Joseph, Jacob dit à Laban : « Laisse-moi partir maintenant, pour que je retourne chez moi, dans mon pays.
fr.R: Quand Rachel a eu Joseph, Jacob a dit à Laban : « Laisse-moi partir maintenant. Je veux retourner chez moi, dans mon pays.

sw.L: Ikawa Raheli alipokwisha kumzaa Yusufu, Yakobo akamwambia Labani, "Niruhusu niondoke, nipate kwenda mahali pangu na nchini kwangu.
sw.B: Baada ya Raheli kumzaa Yusufu, Yakobo alimwambia Labani, "Niruhusu niondoke sasa, ili nirudi nyumbani kwangu na katika nchi yangu.
sw.R: Raheli alipomzaa Yusufu, Yakobo alimwambia Labani, "Niache niondoke sasa. Nataka kurudi nyumbani kwangu, katika nchi yangu.

decisions.choice: when Rachel had borne Joseph: the end of Jacob's service
decisions.reason: Jacob's second seven years of service for Rachel are now over (29:27-30; 31:41). With a son from the wife he loved, he is ready to go home.

source.text: תְּנָ֞ה אֶת־נָשַׁ֣י וְאֶת־יְלָדַ֗י אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָבַ֧דְתִּי אֹֽתְךָ֛ בָּהֵ֖ן וְאֵלֵ֑כָה כִּ֚י אַתָּ֣ה יָדַ֔עְתָּ אֶת־עֲבֹדָתִ֖י אֲשֶׁ֥ר עֲבַדְתִּֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Give [me] my wives and my children, for whom I have served you for them, and I will go; for you, you know my service with which I have served you.

en.L: Give me my wives and my children, for whom I have served you, and let me go, for you yourself know the service I have rendered you."
en.B: Let me take my wives and my children, for whom I served you, and go. You yourself know the work I have done for you."
en.R: Give me my wives and children. I worked for you to earn them. Let me go. You know how hard I have worked for you."

es.L: Dame mis mujeres y mis hijos, por quienes te he servido, y me iré; porque tú sabes el servicio que te he prestado».
es.B: Déjame llevar a mis mujeres y a mis hijos, por los que te he servido, y me iré. Tú mismo sabes el trabajo que he hecho para ti».
es.R: Dame a mis esposas y a mis hijos. Trabajé para ti para ganármelos. Déjame ir. Tú sabes lo mucho que he trabajado para ti».

fr.L: Donne-moi mes femmes et mes enfants, pour lesquels je t’ai servi, et que je m’en aille ; car toi, tu connais le service que je t’ai rendu. »
fr.B: Laisse-moi prendre mes femmes et mes enfants, pour lesquels je t’ai servi, et partir. Tu sais bien, toi, le travail que j’ai fait pour toi. »
fr.R: Donne-moi mes femmes et mes enfants. J’ai travaillé pour toi pour les avoir. Laisse-moi partir. Tu sais combien j’ai travaillé dur pour toi. »

sw.L: Nipe wake zangu na watoto wangu, ambao kwa ajili yao nimekutumikia, nami niende; kwa maana wewe mwenyewe unajua utumishi wangu niliokutumikia."
sw.B: Niruhusu niwachukue wake zangu na watoto wangu, ambao niliwatumikia kwa ajili yao, niende zangu. Wewe mwenyewe unajua kazi niliyokufanyia."
sw.R: Nipe wake zangu na watoto wangu. Nilikufanyia kazi ili niwapate. Niache niende. Unajua jinsi nilivyokufanyia kazi kwa bidii."

decisions.choice: Give me my wives and my children: Laban's claim on them
decisions.reason: Jacob asks for leave as a hired worker who had married into the household. Laban would later claim that the daughters, the grandchildren and the flocks were still his (31:43).

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ לָבָ֔ן אִם־נָ֛א מָצָ֥אתִי חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינֶ֑יךָ נִחַ֕שְׁתִּי וַיְבָרֲכֵ֥נִי יְהוָ֖ה בִּגְלָלֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to him Laban, if please I have found favor in your eyes, I have learned by divination that has blessed me YHWH on account of you.

en.L: And Laban said to him, "If now I have found favor in your eyes, [stay;] I have learned by divination that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has blessed me because of you."
en.B: But Laban said to him, "If you are well disposed toward me, stay. I have learned by omens that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has blessed me because of you."
en.R: But Laban said to him, "Please do me a favor and stay. I have found out by reading signs that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has blessed me because of you."

es.L: Y le dijo Labán: «Si ahora he hallado gracia ante tus ojos, [quédate]; he sabido por adivinación que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me ha bendecido por causa de ti».
es.B: Pero Labán le dijo: «Si me tienes aprecio, quédate. He sabido por presagios que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me ha bendecido gracias a ti».
es.R: Pero Labán le dijo: «Hazme el favor de quedarte. He descubierto, leyendo señales, que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me ha bendecido gracias a ti».

fr.L: Et Laban lui dit : « Si maintenant j’ai trouvé grâce à tes yeux, [reste] ; j’ai appris par divination que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} m’a béni à cause de toi. »
fr.B: Mais Laban lui dit : « Si tu as de la bienveillance pour moi, reste. J’ai appris par des présages que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} m’a béni grâce à toi. »
fr.R: Mais Laban lui a dit : « S’il te plaît, fais-moi plaisir et reste. J’ai découvert en lisant des signes que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} m’a béni grâce à toi. »

sw.L: Labani akamwambia, "Ikiwa sasa nimepata kibali machoni pako, [kaa]; nimetambua kwa uaguzi kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amenibariki kwa ajili yako."
sw.B: Lakini Labani akamwambia, "Kama una nia njema kwangu, tafadhali kaa. Nimetambua kwa ishara za uaguzi kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amenibariki kwa sababu yako."
sw.R: Lakini Labani akamwambia, "Tafadhali nifanyie wema, ubaki. Nimegundua kwa kusoma ishara kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amenibariki kwa sababu yako."

decisions.choice: I have learned by divination: or "I have grown rich"
alternatives: I have grown rich, and the LORD has blessed me
decisions.reason: The verb (nichesh) normally means to practice divination, reading signs and omens (44:5, 15), which the Law later forbids (Leviticus 19:26). A word in a related language means "to prosper", and some take it so here. The common meaning is followed.

decisions.choice: If now I have found favor in your eyes: a sentence left unfinished
decisions.reason: Laban begins a polite request and breaks off; what he wants ("stay") is understood from the context.

decisions.choice: the LORD has blessed me because of you: the promise at work
decisions.reason: God had promised that through Abraham's family others would be blessed (12:3; 28:14). Even Laban sees it, as Potiphar later does with Joseph (39:5).

decisions.choice: [stay] (L); stay (B, R)
decisions.reason: English supplies the request Laban leaves unspoken (m2).

source.text: וַיֹּאמַ֑ר נָקְבָ֧ה שְׂכָרְךָ֛ עָלַ֖י וְאֶתֵּֽנָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, name your wage to me, and I will give [it].

en.L: And he said, "Name your wages to me, and I will give it."
en.B: He went on, "Tell me what wages you want, and I will give them."
en.R: He said, "Tell me what you want me to pay you, and I will pay it."

es.L: Y dijo: «Señálame tu salario, y lo daré».
es.B: Y añadió: «Dime qué salario quieres, y te lo daré».
es.R: Le dijo: «Dime cuánto quieres que te pague, y te lo pagaré».

fr.L: Et il dit : « Fixe-moi ton salaire, et je [le] donnerai. »
fr.B: Il ajouta : « Dis-moi quel salaire tu veux, et je te le donnerai. »
fr.R: Il a dit : « Dis-moi combien tu veux que je te paie, et je te paierai. »

sw.L: Akasema, "Nitajie ujira wako, nami nitautoa."
sw.B: Akaendelea kusema, "Niambie unataka ujira gani, nami nitakupa."
sw.R: Akasema, "Niambie unataka nikulipe nini, nami nitakulipa."

decisions.choice: Name your wages: Laban's offer of 29:15
decisions.reason: Laban made the same offer twenty years before, and it ended with Jacob working fourteen years for his wives. Jacob has learned to be careful (31:7).

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו אַתָּ֣ה יָדַ֔עְתָּ אֵ֖ת אֲשֶׁ֣ר עֲבַדְתִּ֑יךָ וְאֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר־הָיָ֥ה מִקְנְךָ֖ אִתִּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to him, you, you know how I have served you, and how has been your livestock with me.

en.L: And he said to him, "You yourself know how I have served you, and how your livestock has fared with me.
en.B: Jacob replied, "You know what my service has been to you, and what has become of your herds while I tended them.
en.R: Jacob answered, "You know how hard I have worked for you. You know how well your animals have done while I took care of them.

es.L: Y él le dijo: «Tú sabes cómo te he servido, y cómo ha estado tu ganado conmigo.
es.B: Jacob respondió: «Tú sabes cuál ha sido mi servicio y qué ha sido de tus rebaños mientras yo los cuidaba.
es.R: Jacob respondió: «Tú sabes lo mucho que he trabajado para ti. Sabes lo bien que les ha ido a tus animales mientras yo los cuidaba.

fr.L: Et il lui dit : « Tu sais, toi, comment je t’ai servi, et ce qu’est devenu ton bétail avec moi.
fr.B: Jacob répondit : « Tu sais comment je t’ai servi, et ce que sont devenus tes troupeaux sous ma garde.
fr.R: Jacob a répondu : « Tu sais combien j’ai travaillé dur pour toi. Tu sais que tes bêtes se sont bien portées pendant que je m’en occupais.

sw.L: Akamwambia, "Wewe mwenyewe unajua jinsi nilivyokutumikia, na jinsi mifugo yako ilivyokuwa pamoja nami.
sw.B: Yakobo akajibu, "Unajua jinsi nilivyokutumikia, na jinsi mifugo yako ilivyostawi nilipokuwa nikiichunga.
sw.R: Yakobo akajibu, "Unajua jinsi nilivyokufanyia kazi kwa bidii. Unajua jinsi wanyama wako walivyostawi nilipokuwa nikiwatunza.

source.text: כִּ֡י מְעַט֩ אֲשֶׁר־הָיָ֨ה לְךָ֤ לְפָנַי֙ וַיִּפְרֹ֣ץ לָרֹ֔ב וַיְבָ֧רֶךְ יְהוָ֛ה אֹתְךָ֖ לְרַגְלִ֑י וְעַתָּ֗ה מָתַ֛י אֶֽעֱשֶׂ֥ה גַם־אָנֹכִ֖י לְבֵיתִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: For little [it was] which belonged to you before me, and it has broken out into abundance, and has blessed YHWH you at my foot; and now, when will I do, I also, for my household?

en.L: For you had little before I came, and it has increased abundantly, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has blessed you at my every step. But now, when shall I provide for my own household also?"
en.B: Before I came you had only a little, and it has multiplied many times over; {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has blessed you with every step I took. But when am I to provide for my own family?"
en.R: When I came, you did not have many animals. Now you have a great many. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has blessed you wherever I went. But when will I be able to take care of my own family?"

es.L: Porque poco [era] lo que tenías antes de mí, y ha crecido en abundancia, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} te ha bendecido a cada paso mío. Y ahora, ¿cuándo trabajaré también yo para mi propia casa?».
es.B: Antes de que yo llegara tenías poco, y se ha multiplicado muchísimo; {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} te ha bendecido a cada paso que yo daba. Pero ¿cuándo voy a mirar por mi propia familia?».
es.R: Cuando llegué, no tenías muchos animales. Ahora tienes muchísimos. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} te ha bendecido por dondequiera que yo iba. Pero ¿cuándo podré cuidar de mi propia familia?».

fr.L: Car tu avais peu avant moi, et cela s’est accru en abondance, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} t’a béni à chacun de mes pas. Et maintenant, quand travaillerai-je, moi aussi, pour ma propre maison ? »
fr.B: Avant mon arrivée, tu avais peu de chose, et cela s’est multiplié considérablement ; {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} t’a béni à chacun de mes pas. Mais quand pourrai-je pourvoir aux besoins de ma propre famille ? »
fr.R: Quand je suis arrivé, tu n’avais pas beaucoup de bêtes. Maintenant, tu en as énormément. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} t’a béni partout où j’allais. Mais quand est-ce que je pourrai m’occuper de ma propre famille ? »

sw.L: Kwa maana ulikuwa na kidogo kabla yangu, nacho kimeongezeka kwa wingi, naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amekubariki kila hatua yangu. Na sasa, nitaishughulikia lini nyumba yangu mwenyewe pia?"
sw.B: Kabla sijaja ulikuwa na kidogo tu, nacho kimeongezeka mara nyingi; {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amekubariki kila hatua niliyopiga. Lakini nitaiangalia lini jamaa yangu mwenyewe?"
sw.R: Nilipofika hukuwa na wanyama wengi. Sasa una wengi sana. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amekubariki kila mahali nilipokwenda. Lakini nitaweza lini kuitunza jamaa yangu mwenyewe?"

decisions.choice: it has increased: literally "it has broken out"
decisions.reason: The verb (parats) pictures growth bursting through its limits, as in the promise of 28:14, "you will spread out". The same word is used of Jacob in verse 43.

decisions.choice: at my every step: literally "at my foot"
decisions.reason: "At my foot" means wherever I went, at every step. Jacob echoes Laban's words in verse 27: the blessing came with him.

source.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר מָ֣ה אֶתֶּן־לָ֑ךְ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יַעֲקֹב֙ לֹא־תִתֶּן־לִ֣י מְא֔וּמָה אִם־תַּֽעֲשֶׂה־לִּי֙ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה אָשׁ֛וּבָה אֶרְעֶ֥ה צֹֽאנְךָ֖ אֶשְׁמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, what will I give to you? And said Jacob, not you will give to me anything; if you will do for me this thing, I will again pasture your flock [and] keep [it].

en.L: And he said, "What shall I give you?" And Jacob said, "You shall not give me anything. If you will do this thing for me, I will again pasture your flock and keep it:
en.B: Laban asked, "What am I to give you?" "Nothing at all," Jacob answered. "Just agree to one condition, and I will once again shepherd your flocks and guard them.
en.R: Laban asked, "What should I pay you?" Jacob answered, "You do not need to pay me anything. Just agree to this one plan. Then I will keep on taking care of your sheep and goats.

es.L: Y él dijo: «¿Qué te daré?». Y dijo Jacob: «No me darás nada. Si haces por mí esta cosa, volveré a apacentar tu rebaño y a guardarlo:
es.B: Labán le preguntó: «¿Qué te voy a dar?». «Nada en absoluto», respondió Jacob. «Solo acepta una condición, y volveré a pastorear tus rebaños y a cuidarlos.
es.R: Labán le preguntó: «¿Cuánto te debo pagar?». Jacob respondió: «No tienes que pagarme nada. Solo acepta este plan. Entonces seguiré cuidando tus ovejas y tus cabras.

fr.L: Et il dit : « Que te donnerai-je ? » Et Jacob dit : « Tu ne me donneras rien. Si tu fais pour moi cette chose-ci, je recommencerai à faire paître ton troupeau et à le garder :
fr.B: Laban demanda : « Que dois-je te donner ? » « Rien du tout, répondit Jacob. Accepte seulement une condition, et je ferai de nouveau paître tes troupeaux et je les garderai.
fr.R: Laban a demandé : « Combien dois-je te payer ? » Jacob a répondu : « Tu n’as rien à me payer. Accepte seulement ce plan. Alors je continuerai à m’occuper de tes moutons et de tes chèvres.

sw.L: Akasema, "Nikupe nini?" Yakobo akasema, "Hutanipa kitu chochote. Ukinifanyia jambo hili, nitarudi kulichunga kundi lako na kulilinda:
sw.B: Labani akauliza, "Nikupe nini?" Yakobo akajibu, "Hakuna kitu. Kubali tu sharti moja, nami nitachunga tena makundi yako na kuyalinda.
sw.R: Labani akauliza, "Nikulipe nini?" Yakobo akajibu, "Huhitaji kunilipa chochote. Kubali tu mpango huu mmoja. Kisha nitaendelea kuwatunza kondoo na mbuzi wako.

decisions.choice: You shall not give me anything: no wages from Laban's hand
decisions.reason: Jacob asks for nothing Laban already owns. His pay will be whatever odd-colored young are born in the future, so Laban cannot cheat him again by changing what he gives (31:7).

decisions.choice: flock: sheep and goats together
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word (tson) covers small livestock, both sheep and goats, as the next verses show.

source.text: אֶֽעֱבֹ֨ר בְּכָל־צֹֽאנְךָ֜ הַיּ֗וֹם הָסֵ֨ר מִשָּׁ֜ם כָּל־שֶׂ֣ה׀נָקֹ֣ד וְטָל֗וּא וְכָל־שֶׂה־חוּם֙ בַּכְּשָׂבִ֔ים וְטָל֥וּא וְנָקֹ֖ד בָּעִזִּ֑ים וְהָיָ֖ה שְׂכָרִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Let me pass through all your flock today, removing from there every lamb speckled and spotted, and every lamb dark among the sheep, and spotted and speckled among the goats; and it will be my wage.

en.L: Let me pass through all your flock today, removing from it every speckled and spotted animal, and every dark one among the lambs, and the spotted and speckled among the goats; and such shall be my wages.
en.B: Today I will pass through all your flocks and set apart every animal that is speckled or spotted: the dark ones among the lambs and the spotted and speckled among the goats. These will be my pay.
en.R: Today I will go through all your flocks. I will take out every sheep that is dark, and every goat that has spots or speckles. Animals like that will be my pay.

es.L: Pasaré hoy por todo tu rebaño, apartando de allí todo animal moteado y manchado, y todo [animal] oscuro entre los corderos, y lo manchado y moteado entre las cabras; y eso será mi salario.
es.B: Hoy recorreré todos tus rebaños y apartaré todo animal moteado o manchado: los oscuros entre los corderos y los manchados y moteados entre las cabras. Esos serán mi paga.
es.R: Hoy voy a recorrer todos tus rebaños. Sacaré todas las ovejas oscuras y todas las cabras con manchas o pintas. Esos animales serán mi paga.

fr.L: Je passerai aujourd’hui parmi tout ton troupeau, en mettant à part toute bête mouchetée et tachetée, et toute bête foncée parmi les agneaux, et ce qui est tacheté et moucheté parmi les chèvres ; et ce sera mon salaire.
fr.B: Aujourd’hui, je passerai parmi tous tes troupeaux et je mettrai à part toutes les bêtes mouchetées ou tachetées : les agneaux foncés, et les chèvres tachetées et mouchetées. Ce sera mon salaire.
fr.R: Aujourd’hui, je vais passer parmi tous tes troupeaux. Je mettrai de côté tous les moutons foncés, et toutes les chèvres qui ont des taches ou des points. Ces bêtes-là seront mon salaire.

sw.L: Nitapita leo katika kundi lako lote, nikiondoa humo kila mnyama mwenye madoadoa na mabaka, na kila aliye mweusi kati ya wanakondoo, na wenye mabaka na madoadoa kati ya mbuzi; na hao watakuwa ujira wangu.
sw.B: Leo nitapita katika makundi yako yote na kutenga kila mnyama mwenye madoadoa au mabaka: walio weusi kati ya wanakondoo, na wenye mabaka na madoadoa kati ya mbuzi. Hao ndio watakaokuwa ujira wangu.
sw.R: Leo nitapita katika makundi yako yote. Nitatoa kila kondoo mweusi, na kila mbuzi mwenye mabaka au madoadoa. Wanyama wa namna hiyo watakuwa ujira wangu.

decisions.choice: speckled, spotted and dark: the rare colors
decisions.reason: In that region sheep were normally white and goats black or dark brown. Dark sheep and spotted or speckled goats were few, so Jacob seems to ask for very little.

decisions.choice: animal: one head of the flock (seh)
decisions.reason: The word seh means a single sheep or goat.

decisions.choice: removing from it: who removes them?
alternatives: remove from it (Laban is to remove them)
decisions.reason: The verb form does not show who removes the animals. Laban does it himself in verse 35, so Jacob may be telling him to set them apart. Either way, only animals born afterward are Jacob's.

decisions.choice: every sheep that is dark, and every goat that has spots or speckles
decisions.reason: Readable puts the colors with the animals they apply to, following verses 33 and 35.

decisions.choice: "madoadoa" (speckled), "mabaka" (spotted), "mweusi" (dark); "milia" (striped) from verse 35
decisions.reason: Swahili has separate words for small flecks (madoadoa), larger patches (mabaka) and stripes (milia), so the Hebrew color terms can be kept apart through the story. "Mweusi" is the ordinary word for a dark or black animal.

source.text: וְעָֽנְתָה־בִּ֤י צִדְקָתִי֙ בְּי֣וֹם מָחָ֔ר כִּֽי־תָב֥וֹא עַל־שְׂכָרִ֖י לְפָנֶ֑יךָ כֹּ֣ל אֲשֶׁר־אֵינֶנּוּ֩ נָקֹ֨ד וְטָל֜וּא בָּֽעִזִּ֗ים וְחוּם֙ בַּכְּשָׂבִ֔ים גָּנ֥וּב ה֖וּא אִתִּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And will answer for me my righteousness on a day to come, when you come about my wage before you: all which not speckled and spotted among the goats and dark among the sheep, stolen it [is] with me.

en.L: And my righteousness will answer for me on a day to come, when you come about my wages before you: every one that is not speckled and spotted among the goats and dark among the lambs, it [shall count as] stolen with me."
en.B: Later on, my honesty will be my witness. Whenever you come to look over my wages, if I have any goat without speckles or spots, or any lamb that is not dark, you may count it as stolen."
en.R: In the future you will see that I am honest. When you come to check the animals you gave me as pay, look at them. If you find any goat that is not spotted or speckled, or any sheep that is not dark, you will know I stole it."

es.L: Y responderá por mí mi justicia en el día de mañana, cuando vengas a causa de mi salario delante de ti: todo lo que no sea moteado y manchado entre las cabras, y oscuro entre los corderos, [será tenido por] robado conmigo».
es.B: Más adelante, mi honradez será mi testigo. Cada vez que vengas a revisar mi paga, si tengo alguna cabra sin motas ni manchas, o algún cordero que no sea oscuro, podrás darlo por robado».
es.R: En el futuro verás que soy honrado. Cuando vengas a revisar los animales que me diste como paga, míralos. Si encuentras alguna cabra que no tenga manchas o pintas, o alguna oveja que no sea oscura, sabrás que la robé».

fr.L: Et ma justice répondra pour moi un jour à venir, quand tu viendras au sujet de mon salaire devant toi : tout ce qui n’est pas moucheté et tacheté parmi les chèvres, et foncé parmi les agneaux, [sera compté comme] volé chez moi. »
fr.B: Plus tard, mon honnêteté témoignera pour moi. Chaque fois que tu viendras examiner mon salaire, si j’ai une chèvre qui n’est ni mouchetée ni tachetée, ou un agneau qui n’est pas foncé, tu pourras le considérer comme volé. »
fr.R: Plus tard, tu verras que je suis honnête. Quand tu viendras vérifier les bêtes que tu m’as données comme salaire, regarde-les. Si tu trouves une chèvre qui n’a ni taches ni points, ou un mouton qui n’est pas foncé, tu sauras que je l’ai volé. »

sw.L: Na haki yangu itanishuhudia siku ijayo, utakapokuja kuhusu ujira wangu mbele yako: kila asiye na madoadoa na mabaka kati ya mbuzi, na mweusi kati ya wanakondoo, [atahesabiwa kuwa] ameibwa kwangu."
sw.B: Baadaye uaminifu wangu utanishuhudia. Kila utakapokuja kukagua ujira wangu, ikiwa nina mbuzi yeyote asiye na madoadoa wala mabaka, au mwanakondoo yeyote asiye mweusi, unaweza kumhesabu kuwa ameibwa."
sw.R: Siku zijazo utaona kwamba mimi ni mwaminifu. Ukija kukagua wanyama ulionipa kama ujira, waangalie. Ukikuta mbuzi yeyote asiye na mabaka au madoadoa, au kondoo yeyote asiye mweusi, utajua kwamba nimemwiba."

decisions.choice: my honesty: literally "my righteousness"
decisions.reason: The word (tsedaqah) here means fairness in dealings, being in the right. The animals' colors will "testify" that Jacob has kept the bargain.

decisions.choice: honesty (B); I am honest (R)
decisions.reason: In a business dealing the word means honest conduct; Balanced and Readable say so, and Literal keeps "righteousness" (m1).

source.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר לָבָ֖ן הֵ֑ן ל֖וּ יְהִ֥י כִדְבָרֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Laban, behold, let it be according to your word.

en.L: And Laban said, "Good! Let it be as you have said."
en.B: Laban said, "Very well, let it be just as you say."
en.R: Laban said, "All right. We will do as you say."

es.L: Y dijo Labán: «¡Bien! Sea conforme a tu palabra».
es.B: Labán dijo: «Muy bien, que sea tal como dices».
es.R: Labán dijo: «De acuerdo. Haremos lo que dices».

fr.L: Et Laban dit : « Bien ! Qu’il en soit selon ta parole. »
fr.B: Laban dit : « Très bien, qu’il en soit comme tu le dis. »
fr.R: Laban a dit : « D’accord. Nous ferons comme tu dis. »

sw.L: Labani akasema, "Vema! Na iwe kama ulivyosema."
sw.B: Labani akasema, "Sawa kabisa, na iwe kama unavyosema."
sw.R: Labani akasema, "Haya. Tutafanya kama unavyosema."

decisions.choice: Good!: literally "look, if only"
decisions.reason: Laban's two words of agreement (hen lu) mean "yes, so be it"; he is quick to accept a bargain that seems to cost him so little.

source.text: וַיָּ֣סַר בַּיּוֹם֩ הַה֨וּא אֶת־הַתְּיָשִׁ֜ים הָֽעֲקֻדִּ֣ים וְהַטְּלֻאִ֗ים וְאֵ֤ת כָּל־הָֽעִזִּים֙ הַנְּקֻדּ֣וֹת וְהַטְּלֻאֹ֔ת כֹּ֤ל אֲשֶׁר־לָבָן֙ בּ֔וֹ וְכָל־ח֖וּם בַּכְּשָׂבִ֑ים וַיִּתֵּ֖ן בְּיַד־בָּנָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And he removed on that day the male goats striped and spotted and all the female goats speckled and spotted, every one that [had] white on it, and every dark one among the sheep, and he gave [them] into [the] hand of his sons.

en.L: But that same day he removed the striped and spotted male goats and all the speckled and spotted female goats, every one with white on it, and every dark one among the lambs, and put them in the charge of his sons.
en.B: But on that very day Laban picked out the male goats with stripes or spots, the female goats with speckles or spots, any with white on them, and every dark lamb, and handed them over to his sons.
en.R: But that same day Laban took away all the male goats that had stripes or spots. He took all the female goats that had speckles or spots, or any white on them. He also took all the dark sheep. He told his sons to take care of them.

es.L: Pero aquel mismo día apartó los machos cabríos rayados y manchados, y todas las cabras moteadas y manchadas, todo lo que tenía blanco, y todo lo oscuro entre los corderos, y los puso en mano de sus hijos.
es.B: Pero aquel mismo día Labán separó los machos cabríos con rayas o manchas, las cabras con motas o manchas, todas las que tenían algo de blanco, y todos los corderos oscuros, y se los entregó a sus hijos.
es.R: Pero ese mismo día Labán se llevó todos los machos cabríos que tenían rayas o manchas. Se llevó todas las cabras que tenían manchas o pintas, o algo de blanco. También se llevó todas las ovejas oscuras. Les dijo a sus hijos que las cuidaran.

fr.L: Mais ce jour-là même, il mit à part les boucs rayés et tachetés, et toutes les chèvres mouchetées et tachetées, toutes celles qui avaient du blanc, et toute bête foncée parmi les agneaux, et il les remit entre les mains de ses fils.
fr.B: Mais ce jour-là même, Laban mit à part les boucs rayés ou tachetés, les chèvres mouchetées ou tachetées, toutes celles qui avaient du blanc, ainsi que tous les agneaux foncés, et il les confia à ses fils.
fr.R: Mais le jour même, Laban a pris tous les boucs qui avaient des rayures ou des taches. Il a pris toutes les chèvres qui avaient des taches ou des points, ou un peu de blanc. Il a pris aussi tous les moutons foncés. Il a demandé à ses fils de s’en occuper.

sw.L: Lakini siku ile ile akaondoa beberu wenye milia na mabaka, na mbuzi wote wa kike wenye madoadoa na mabaka, kila mmoja aliyekuwa na weupe juu yake, na kila mweusi kati ya wanakondoo, akawatia mikononi mwa wanawe.
sw.B: Lakini siku ile ile Labani aliwatenga beberu wenye milia au mabaka, mbuzi wa kike wenye madoadoa au mabaka, wote waliokuwa na weupe, na kila mwanakondoo mweusi, akawakabidhi wanawe.
sw.R: Lakini siku ile ile Labani aliwachukua beberu wote wenye milia au mabaka. Akawachukua mbuzi wote wa kike wenye mabaka au madoadoa, au wenye weupe wowote. Akawachukua pia kondoo wote weusi. Akawaambia wanawe wawatunze.

decisions.choice: he removed: Laban takes the colored animals for himself
decisions.reason: "He" is Laban. He gives the colored animals to his own sons and sends them far away (verse 36), so that Jacob is left with only white sheep and dark goats, from which few colored young would be expected.

decisions.choice: white (lavan): a pun on Laban
decisions.reason: The word for white is the same as Laban's name. The story plays on it in verse 37 too: Laban the "white" is outwitted by white-peeled sticks.

decisions.choice: But (B, R); Laban (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable mark the contrast with Laban's agreement, and Readable names him.

source.text: וַיָּ֗שֶׂם דֶּ֚רֶךְ שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֔ים בֵּינ֖וֹ וּבֵ֣ין יַעֲקֹ֑ב וְיַעֲקֹ֗ב רֹעֶ֛ה אֶת־צֹ֥אן לָבָ֖ן הַנּוֹתָרֹֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And he put [a] journey of three days between himself and Jacob; and Jacob [was] pasturing the flock of Laban which remained.

en.L: And he put a three days' journey between himself and Jacob, and Jacob pastured the rest of Laban's flock.
en.B: He then moved them a three days' journey away from Jacob, and Jacob was left to pasture the rest of Laban's flocks.
en.R: Laban took these animals three days' journey away from Jacob. Jacob went on taking care of the rest of Laban's flocks.

es.L: Y puso un camino de tres días entre él y Jacob; y Jacob apacentaba el resto del rebaño de Labán.
es.B: Luego los llevó a tres días de camino de Jacob, y Jacob se quedó apacentando el resto de los rebaños de Labán.
es.R: Labán se llevó esos animales a tres días de camino de Jacob. Jacob siguió cuidando el resto de los rebaños de Labán.

fr.L: Et il mit trois jours de chemin entre lui et Jacob ; et Jacob faisait paître le reste du troupeau de Laban.
fr.B: Puis il les emmena à trois jours de marche de Jacob, et Jacob resta à faire paître le reste des troupeaux de Laban.
fr.R: Laban a emmené ces bêtes à trois jours de marche de Jacob. Jacob a continué à s’occuper du reste des troupeaux de Laban.

sw.L: Akaweka mwendo wa siku tatu kati yake na Yakobo; naye Yakobo akachunga kundi la Labani lililobaki.
sw.B: Kisha akawapeleka mbali, mwendo wa siku tatu kutoka kwa Yakobo, naye Yakobo akabaki akichunga makundi ya Labani yaliyosalia.
sw.R: Labani aliwapeleka wanyama hao mwendo wa siku tatu mbali na Yakobo. Yakobo akaendelea kutunza makundi mengine ya Labani.

source.text: וַיִּֽקַּֽח־ל֣וֹ יַעֲקֹ֗ב מַקַּ֥ל לִבְנֶ֛ה לַ֖ח וְל֣וּז וְעֶרְמ֑וֹןוַיְפַצֵּ֤ל בָּהֵן֙ פְּצָל֣וֹת לְבָנ֔וֹת מַחְשֹׂף֙ הַלָּבָ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־הַמַּקְלֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And took for himself Jacob branch[es] of poplar fresh, and almond, and plane tree, and he peeled on them white strips, laying bare the white which [was] on the branches.

en.L: And Jacob took for himself fresh branches of poplar and almond and plane tree, and peeled white stripes in them, laying bare the white that was in the branches.
en.B: Jacob then took freshly cut sticks of poplar, almond and plane wood and peeled bark off them in strips, baring the white wood underneath.
en.R: Then Jacob cut some fresh branches from poplar, almond and plane trees. He peeled off strips of bark so that the branches had white stripes on them.

es.L: Y tomó Jacob para sí varas verdes de álamo, de almendro y de plátano, y descortezó en ellas tiras blancas, dejando al descubierto lo blanco que había en las varas.
es.B: Jacob tomó entonces varas recién cortadas de álamo, de almendro y de plátano oriental, y les quitó la corteza a tiras, dejando a la vista la madera blanca de debajo.
es.R: Entonces Jacob cortó unas ramas frescas de álamo, de almendro y de plátano. Les quitó tiras de corteza para que las ramas quedaran con rayas blancas.

fr.L: Et Jacob prit pour lui des branches fraîches de peuplier, d’amandier et de platane, et il y pela des bandes blanches, mettant à nu le blanc qui était dans les branches.
fr.B: Jacob prit ensuite des baguettes fraîchement coupées de peuplier, d’amandier et de platane, et en ôta l’écorce par bandes, mettant à nu le bois blanc qui se trouvait dessous.
fr.R: Ensuite, Jacob a coupé des branches fraîches de peupliers, d’amandiers et de platanes. Il a enlevé des bandes d’écorce, pour que les branches aient des rayures blanches.

sw.L: Yakobo akajitwalia fimbo mbichi za mpopla, na za mlozi, na za mwaramoni, akabambua juu yake milia myeupe, akiufunua weupe uliokuwa ndani ya fimbo.
sw.B: Kisha Yakobo alichukua fimbo zilizokatwa karibuni za mpopla, za mlozi na za mwaramoni, akabambua magome yake kwa milia, akaufunua mti mweupe uliokuwa chini yake.
sw.R: Kisha Yakobo akakata matawi mabichi ya mpopla, ya mlozi na ya mwaramoni. Akabambua vipande vya maganda ili matawi yawe na milia myeupe.

decisions.choice: poplar (livneh), white (lavan): more puns on Laban
decisions.reason: The word for poplar, the white stripes and the white wood all sound like Laban's name. Laban, "white", who had taken away every animal with white on it (verse 35), is beaten with white.

decisions.choice: almond and plane tree
decisions.reason: The almond (luz) has the same name as the town Luz, the old name of Bethel (28:19). The plane tree (ermon) is a tall tree with bark that peels in patches.

decisions.choice: "mpopla" (poplar), "mlozi" (almond), "mwaramoni" (plane tree)
alternatives: a general "miti ya aina tatu" (three kinds of tree)
decisions.reason: "Mlozi" is the ordinary Swahili almond tree. The poplar and the plane tree do not grow in East Africa and have no everyday Swahili names, so the poplar is given the borrowed name and the plane tree a form of its Hebrew name (ermon). The pun on Laban's name (lavan, livneh) cannot be kept in Swahili; "milia myeupe" and "weupe" keep the stress on whiteness.

source.text: וַיַּצֵּ֗ג אֶת־הַמַּקְלוֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר פִּצֵּ֔ל בָּרֳהָטִ֖ים בְּשִֽׁקֲת֣וֹת הַמָּ֑יִם אֲשֶׁר֩ תָּבֹ֨אןָ הַצֹּ֤אן לִשְׁתּוֹת֙ לְנֹ֣כַח הַצֹּ֔אן וַיֵּחַ֖מְנָה בְּבֹאָ֥ן לִשְׁתּֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And he set the branches which he had peeled in the troughs, in the watering channels, where came the flock to drink, in front of the flock; and they were in heat when they came to drink.

en.L: And he set the branches that he had peeled in front of the flock in the troughs, at the watering places where the flock came to drink. And they mated when they came to drink.
en.B: He set the peeled sticks in the troughs at the watering places, right in front of the animals as they came to drink, for they came into heat when they came to drink.
en.R: He put the peeled branches in the water troughs where the animals came to drink. The branches were right in front of them. The animals were ready to mate when they came to drink.

es.L: Y puso las varas que había descortezado delante del rebaño en los abrevaderos, en los canales del agua, adonde venía el rebaño a beber; y entraban en celo cuando venían a beber.
es.B: Colocó las varas descortezadas en los abrevaderos, justo delante de los animales cuando venían a beber, porque entraban en celo cuando venían a beber.
es.R: Puso las ramas descortezadas en los abrevaderos donde los animales iban a beber. Las ramas quedaban justo delante de ellos. Los animales estaban listos para aparearse cuando venían a beber.

fr.L: Et il plaça les branches qu’il avait pelées devant le troupeau, dans les auges, aux abreuvoirs où le troupeau venait boire ; et elles s’accouplaient quand elles venaient boire.
fr.B: Il plaça les baguettes pelées dans les auges, aux abreuvoirs, juste devant les bêtes quand elles venaient boire, car elles entraient en chaleur en venant boire.
fr.R: Il a mis les branches pelées dans les abreuvoirs où les bêtes venaient boire. Les branches étaient juste devant elles. Les bêtes étaient prêtes à s’accoupler quand elles venaient boire.

sw.L: Akaziweka fimbo alizozibambua mbele ya kundi katika mabirika, katika mifereji ya maji, mahali kundi lilipokuja kunywa; nao wakapandana walipokuja kunywa.
sw.B: Aliziweka fimbo zilizobambuliwa katika mabirika ya kunyweshea, mbele kabisa ya wanyama walipokuja kunywa, kwa maana walikuwa na hamu ya kupandana walipokuja kunywa.
sw.R: Aliweka matawi yaliyobambuliwa katika mabirika ya maji ambapo wanyama walikuja kunywa. Matawi yalikuwa mbele yao kabisa. Wanyama walikuwa tayari kupandana walipokuja kunywa.

decisions.choice: they mated: they came into heat
decisions.reason: The verb (yacham) means to be in heat, warm with desire. When the animals gathered at the water they were ready to breed, and Jacob chose that moment.

source.text: וַיֶּחֱמ֥וּ הַצֹּ֖אן אֶל־הַמַּקְל֑וֹת וַתֵּלַ֣דְןָ הַצֹּ֔אן עֲקֻדִּ֥ים נְקֻדִּ֖ים וּטְלֻאִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And were in heat the flock at the branches, and bore the flock striped, speckled, and spotted.

en.L: And the flocks mated in front of the branches, and the flocks bore young that were striped, speckled and spotted.
en.B: The flocks bred in front of the sticks, and their young were born striped, speckled and spotted.
en.R: The animals mated in front of the branches. Then they gave birth to young ones with stripes, speckles and spots.

es.L: Y se apareaban los rebaños delante de las varas, y los rebaños parían [crías] rayadas, moteadas y manchadas.
es.B: Los rebaños se apareaban delante de las varas, y sus crías nacían rayadas, moteadas y manchadas.
es.R: Los animales se aparearon delante de las ramas. Luego tuvieron crías con rayas, pintas y manchas.

fr.L: Et les troupeaux s’accouplèrent devant les branches, et les troupeaux mirent bas [des petits] rayés, mouchetés et tachetés.
fr.B: Les bêtes s’accouplaient devant les baguettes, et leurs petits naissaient rayés, mouchetés et tachetés.
fr.R: Les bêtes se sont accouplées devant les branches. Ensuite, elles ont eu des petits avec des rayures, des points et des taches.

sw.L: Makundi yakapandana mbele ya fimbo, nayo makundi yakazaa [wana] wenye milia, madoadoa na mabaka.
sw.B: Makundi yalipandana mbele ya fimbo, na wana wao wakazaliwa na milia, madoadoa na mabaka.
sw.R: Wanyama walipandana mbele ya matawi. Kisha wakazaa wana wenye milia, madoadoa na mabaka.

decisions.choice: the branches and the colored young: what caused it?
decisions.reason: People of that time believed that what a mother saw at the moment of conceiving could mark her young. The narrator reports what Jacob did and what followed, without endorsing the method. Jacob later says that God gave him the flocks and showed him in a dream which males would mate (31:9-12); the true cause was God's blessing, not the sticks.

source.text: וְהַכְּשָׂבִים֮ הִפְרִ֣יד יַעֲקֹב֒ וַ֠יִּתֵּן פְּנֵ֨י הַצֹּ֧אן אֶל־עָקֹ֛ד וְכָל־ח֖וּם בְּצֹ֣אן לָבָ֑ן וַיָּֽשֶׁת־ל֤וֹ עֲדָרִים֙ לְבַדּ֔וֹ וְלֹ֥א שָׁתָ֖ם עַל־צֹ֥אן לָבָֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And the lambs separated Jacob, and he set [the] faces of the flock toward [the] striped and every dark one in [the] flock of Laban; and he made for himself flocks by himself, and not he put them with [the] flock of Laban.

en.L: And Jacob separated the lambs, and set the faces of the flock toward the striped and all the dark ones in Laban's flock. And he put his own droves apart by themselves and did not put them with Laban's flock.
en.B: Jacob kept the lambs apart, but turned the animals to face the striped and dark ones in Laban's flock. In this way he built up flocks of his own, which he kept apart from Laban's.
en.R: Jacob separated the young animals. He made the rest of the flock face the striped and dark animals in Laban's flock. In this way Jacob built up his own flocks and kept them away from Laban's animals.

es.L: Y Jacob apartó los corderos, y puso la cara del rebaño hacia lo rayado y todo lo oscuro en el rebaño de Labán. Y puso sus propios hatos aparte, y no los puso con el rebaño de Labán.
es.B: Jacob mantenía aparte los corderos, pero hacía que los animales miraran hacia los rayados y oscuros del rebaño de Labán. Así formó rebaños propios, que mantuvo separados de los de Labán.
es.R: Jacob separó a los animales jóvenes. Hizo que el resto del rebaño mirara hacia los animales rayados y oscuros del rebaño de Labán. Así Jacob formó sus propios rebaños y los mantuvo lejos de los animales de Labán.

fr.L: Et Jacob sépara les agneaux, et il tourna la face du troupeau vers ce qui était rayé et tout ce qui était foncé dans le troupeau de Laban. Et il mit ses propres troupeaux à part et ne les mit pas avec le troupeau de Laban.
fr.B: Jacob tenait les agneaux à part, mais il tournait les bêtes vers celles qui étaient rayées ou foncées dans le troupeau de Laban. Il se constitua ainsi des troupeaux à lui, qu’il gardait à l’écart de ceux de Laban.
fr.R: Jacob a séparé les jeunes bêtes. Il a fait en sorte que le reste du troupeau regarde les bêtes rayées et foncées du troupeau de Laban. De cette manière, Jacob s’est fait ses propres troupeaux et les a gardés loin des bêtes de Laban.

sw.L: Yakobo akawatenga wanakondoo, akazielekeza nyuso za kundi kuelekea wenye milia na wote weusi katika kundi la Labani. Akayaweka makundi yake mwenyewe peke yake, wala hakuyaweka pamoja na kundi la Labani.
sw.B: Yakobo aliwaweka wanakondoo mbali, lakini akawageuza wanyama watazame wale wenye milia na weusi katika kundi la Labani. Kwa njia hiyo akajipatia makundi yake mwenyewe, akayaweka mbali na ya Labani.
sw.R: Yakobo aliwatenga wanyama wachanga. Akawafanya wanyama wengine watazame wanyama wenye milia na weusi katika kundi la Labani. Kwa njia hiyo Yakobo alijipatia makundi yake mwenyewe, akayaweka mbali na wanyama wa Labani.

decisions.choice: the sense of the verse is not clear
alternatives: Jacob separated the lambs, and turned the flock toward Laban's striped and dark animals
decisions.reason: The verse is compressed, and it is not certain which animals were separated or which faced which. The likely sense is that Jacob kept the colored young that were his apart, but let the breeding animals see them, so that more colored young would be born; and he kept his growing flock away from Laban's.

source.text: וְהָיָ֗ה בְּכָל־יַחֵם֮ הַצֹּ֣אן הַמְקֻשָּׁרוֹת֒ וְשָׂ֨ם יַעֲקֹ֧ב אֶת־הַמַּקְל֛וֹת לְעֵינֵ֥י הַצֹּ֖אן בָּרֳהָטִ֑ים לְיַחְמֵ֖נָּה בַּמַּקְלֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, in every mating of the flock, the strong ones, and put Jacob the branches before the eyes of the flock in the troughs, that they might mate among the branches;

en.L: And whenever the stronger of the flock were mating, Jacob would lay the branches in the troughs before the eyes of the flock, so that they would mate among the branches;
en.B: Each time the sturdier animals were mating, Jacob laid the sticks in the troughs in full view of the flock, so that they bred among the sticks;
en.R: Whenever the strong, healthy animals were ready to mate, Jacob put the branches in the troughs in front of them. That way they mated near the branches.

es.L: Y sucedía que, cada vez que se apareaban los más robustos del rebaño, Jacob ponía las varas en los abrevaderos delante de los ojos del rebaño, para que se aparearan entre las varas;
es.B: Cada vez que los animales más fuertes se apareaban, Jacob ponía las varas en los abrevaderos a la vista del rebaño, para que se cruzaran entre las varas;
es.R: Cada vez que los animales fuertes y sanos estaban listos para aparearse, Jacob ponía las ramas en los abrevaderos delante de ellos. Así se apareaban cerca de las ramas.

fr.L: Et il arrivait, chaque fois que les plus vigoureuses du troupeau s’accouplaient, que Jacob mettait les branches dans les auges sous les yeux du troupeau, pour qu’elles s’accouplent parmi les branches ;
fr.B: Chaque fois que les bêtes les plus robustes s’accouplaient, Jacob plaçait les baguettes dans les auges, bien en vue du troupeau, pour qu’elles s’accouplent au milieu des baguettes ;
fr.R: Chaque fois que les bêtes fortes et en bonne santé étaient prêtes à s’accoupler, Jacob mettait les branches dans les abreuvoirs devant elles. Comme ça, elles s’accouplaient près des branches.

sw.L: Ikawa kila mara wanyama wenye nguvu wa kundi walipopandana, Yakobo aliziweka fimbo katika mabirika mbele ya macho ya kundi, ili wapandane katikati ya fimbo;
sw.B: Kila mara wanyama wenye nguvu zaidi walipopandana, Yakobo aliziweka fimbo katika mabirika mahali ambapo kundi lingeziona waziwazi, ili wapandane katikati ya fimbo;
sw.R: Kila mara wanyama wenye nguvu na afya walipokuwa tayari kupandana, Yakobo aliweka matawi katika mabirika mbele yao. Kwa hiyo walipandana karibu na matawi.

decisions.choice: the stronger: literally "the bound ones"
alternatives: the ones bred early in the season
decisions.reason: The word (mequsharot) seems to mean firm or sturdy, strong animals. Some take it to mean the animals that bred in the spring, when stronger young were born.

source.text: וּבְהַעֲטִ֥יף הַצֹּ֖אן לֹ֣א יָשִׂ֑ים וְהָיָ֤ה הָעֲטֻפִים֙ לְלָבָ֔ן וְהַקְּשֻׁרִ֖ים לְיַעֲקֹֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: and in the feebleness of the flock, not he put [them]; and were the feeble [ones] to Laban and the strong [ones] to Jacob.

en.L: but when the flock was feeble he did not put them there. So the feebler ones were Laban's and the stronger Jacob's.
en.B: but when the weaker animals mated, he left the sticks out. In this way the feeble animals ended up as Laban's and the strong ones as Jacob's.
en.R: But when the weak animals were ready to mate, he did not put out the branches. So Laban got the weak animals, and Jacob got the strong ones.

es.L: pero cuando el rebaño estaba débil, no las ponía. Así, los más débiles eran de Labán, y los más robustos de Jacob.
es.B: pero cuando se apareaban los animales más débiles, no ponía las varas. De este modo, los débiles quedaban para Labán y los fuertes para Jacob.
es.R: Pero cuando los animales débiles estaban listos para aparearse, no ponía las ramas. Así Labán se quedó con los animales débiles, y Jacob con los fuertes.

fr.L: mais quand le troupeau était chétif, il ne les mettait pas. Ainsi les plus chétives étaient pour Laban, et les plus vigoureuses pour Jacob.
fr.B: mais quand c’étaient les bêtes les plus faibles, il ne mettait pas les baguettes. Ainsi les bêtes chétives revenaient à Laban, et les robustes à Jacob.
fr.R: Mais quand les bêtes faibles étaient prêtes à s’accoupler, il ne mettait pas les branches. Comme ça, Laban a eu les bêtes faibles, et Jacob les bêtes fortes.

sw.L: lakini kundi lilipokuwa dhaifu hakuziweka. Hivyo walio dhaifu wakawa wa Labani, na wenye nguvu wa Yakobo.
sw.B: lakini wanyama dhaifu walipopandana, hakuziweka fimbo. Kwa njia hiyo wanyama dhaifu wakawa wa Labani, na wenye nguvu wakawa wa Yakobo.
sw.R: Lakini wanyama dhaifu walipokuwa tayari kupandana, hakuweka matawi. Kwa hiyo Labani alipata wanyama dhaifu, na Yakobo akapata wenye nguvu.

source.text: וַיִּפְרֹ֥ץ הָאִ֖ישׁ מְאֹ֣ד מְאֹ֑ד וַֽיְהִי־לוֹ֙ צֹ֣אן רַבּ֔וֹת וּשְׁפָחוֹת֙ וַעֲבָדִ֔ים וּגְמַלִּ֖ים וַחֲמֹרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And increased the man very very, and there were to him flocks many and female slaves and male slaves and camels and donkeys.

en.L: And the man grew exceedingly rich and had many flocks, and female and male slaves, and camels and donkeys.
en.B: So Jacob grew richer and richer. He came to own great flocks, servants both female and male, camels and donkeys.
en.R: So Jacob became very, very rich. He had large flocks of sheep and goats, many servants, and camels and donkeys.

es.L: Y el hombre se enriqueció muchísimo, y tuvo muchos rebaños, y esclavas y esclavos, y camellos y asnos.
es.B: Así Jacob se fue haciendo cada vez más rico. Llegó a tener grandes rebaños, siervas y siervos, camellos y asnos.
es.R: Así Jacob llegó a ser muy, muy rico. Tenía grandes rebaños de ovejas y cabras, muchos siervos, y camellos y burros.

fr.L: Et l’homme s’enrichit extrêmement, et il eut de nombreux troupeaux, et des esclaves, femmes et hommes, et des chameaux et des ânes.
fr.B: Jacob devint ainsi de plus en plus riche. Il posséda de grands troupeaux, des servantes et des serviteurs, des chameaux et des ânes.
fr.R: Jacob est donc devenu très, très riche. Il avait de grands troupeaux de moutons et de chèvres, beaucoup de serviteurs, des chameaux et des ânes.

sw.L: Mtu huyo akastawi sana sana, akawa na makundi mengi, na watumwa wa kike na wa kiume, na ngamia na punda.
sw.B: Hivyo Yakobo akazidi kutajirika. Akawa na makundi makubwa, watumishi wa kike na wa kiume, ngamia na punda.
sw.R: Basi Yakobo akawa tajiri sana sana. Alikuwa na makundi makubwa ya kondoo na mbuzi, watumishi wengi, ngamia na punda.

decisions.choice: the man grew exceedingly rich: the promise fulfilled
decisions.reason: The verb is the "break out" of verse 30 and of God's promise at Bethel, "you will spread out" (28:14). Jacob now has the kind of wealth Abraham (12:16) and Isaac (26:13-14) had.

decisions.choice: female and male slaves
decisions.reason: The words (shifchah, eved) are the usual words for owned servants, as with Abraham's household (12:16).

decisions.choice: grew exceedingly rich
decisions.reason: The repeated "very" is a Hebrew way to say "extremely"; each level gives it in English form.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servants" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); the meaning decision (m2) keeps that they were owned, and Literal keeps "slave".
